Topics · The holy books together

Are Jews the chosen people?

God favoured the Children of Israel, the Quran says. It asks what any favour rests on, and tests Muslims too.

Part 1 of 4

﴿يَـٰبَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱذْكُرُوا۟ نِعْمَتِىَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَنْعَمْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَأَنِّى فَضَّلْتُكُمْ عَلَى ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O Children of Israel, remember My favor that I have bestowed upon you and that I preferred you over the worlds [i.e., peoples].

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:47

﴿وَلَقَدِ ٱخْتَرْنَـٰهُمْ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ عَلَى ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We certainly chose them by knowledge over [all] the worlds.

Quran · Ad-Dukhan 44:32

Begin where the Quran begins. It says, in God's voice, that He favoured the Children of Israel above the worlds, and it says so again. Elsewhere it says He chose them knowingly. These words are not given grudgingly, and a reader expecting the Quran to deny the choosing will not find that here. The question it raises is the one Jewish tradition raises: chosen for what? A favour says something about the giver. What it asks of the one who receives it comes next.

A question for you

When you hear the word chosen, what do you hear first?

If you sayA task
ThenThat is the answer of many Jewish teachers: chosen for Torah and for service. Then the word speaks of duty. The next verse asks what happens to a duty when it is inherited.
If you sayA love that does not end
ThenMany Jews hold to that, and the prophets speak of a love that outlasts failure. Keep hold of that as you read on.
If you sayA word I am uneasy with
ThenMany Jewish readers share that unease, since the word has brought suspicion as well as honour. Let us see how it is reasoned through here, calmly.

Part 2 of 4

﴿وَإِذِ ٱبْتَلَىٰٓ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَـٰتٍ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّ ۖ قَالَ إِنِّى جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامًا ۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِى ۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهْدِى ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention, O Muḥammad], when Abraham was tried by his Lord with words [i.e., commands] and he fulfilled them. [Allāh] said, "Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people." [Abraham] said, "And of my descendants?" [Allāh] said, "My covenant does not include the wrongdoers."

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:124

Translation

Your name will no more be called Abram, but your name will be Abraham; for I have made you the father of a multitude of nations.

Original · Hebrew

וְלֹא־יִקָּרֵ֥א ע֛וֹד אֶת־שִׁמְךָ֖ אַבְרָ֑ם וְהָיָ֤ה שִׁמְךָ֙ אַבְרָהָ֔ם כִּ֛י אַב־הֲמ֥וֹן גּוֹיִ֖ם נְתַתִּֽיךָ׃

the Torah (Genesis) · 17:5

World English Bible

Abraham is tested and completes the test, and God makes him a leader for the people. He asks the natural question: and my children? The answer is short: My covenant does not reach those who do wrong. Notice what it leaves unsaid. It does not cancel his descendants. It distinguishes. Descent gives a place in the story, and does not by itself give the covenant's promise. This was said of all Abraham's children, through both his sons.

A question for you

Set this beside what the prophets of Israel said about its calling. Which is closest to your view?

If you sayIt is what Amos and Jeremiah say
ThenThen the Quran and the prophets make one demanding point: to be known by God is to be asked for more.
If you sayThe covenant is eternal and cannot be lost
ThenThat is a central Jewish teaching, with strong texts. The verse speaks of whom the covenant reaches, and the next verses put every reader under the same measure.
If you sayIt applies to everyone, not only to Jews
ThenIt does, and the next verses say so plainly, to Muslims first.

﴿وَقَالَتِ ٱلْيَهُودُ وَٱلنَّصَـٰرَىٰ نَحْنُ أَبْنَـٰٓؤُا۟ ٱللَّهِ وَأَحِبَّـٰٓؤُهُۥ ۚ قُلْ فَلِمَ يُعَذِّبُكُم بِذُنُوبِكُم ۖ بَلْ أَنتُم بَشَرٌ مِّمَّنْ خَلَقَ ۚ يَغْفِرُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيُعَذِّبُ مَن يَشَآءُ ۚ وَلِلَّهِ مُلْكُ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا ۖ وَإِلَيْهِ ٱلْمَصِيرُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But the Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allāh and His beloved." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins?" Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And to Allāh belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:18

Translation

Are you not like the children of the Ethiopians to me, children of Israel?” says Yahweh. “Haven’t I brought up Israel out of the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and the Syrians from Kir?

Original · Hebrew

הֲל֣וֹא כִבְנֵי֩ כֻשִׁיִּ֨ים אַתֶּ֥ם לִ֛י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה הֲל֣וֹא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הֶעֱלֵ֨יתִי֙ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וּפְלִשְׁתִּיִּ֥ים מִכַּפְתּ֖וֹר וַאֲרָ֥ם מִקִּֽיר׃

Amos · 9:7

World English Bible

Every community is tempted to think God is with it because it is itself. The first verse says this to the Quran's own readers: it is not by your wishes, nor by the wishes of the People of the Book, and whoever does wrong answers for it. The second reports the same feeling among Jews and Christians, that they are God's children and beloved, and replies: you are people, among those He created. That is level ground for everyone. Belonging is a comfort, and each person brings their own deeds.

A question for you

What does your tradition say about the righteous outside Israel?

If you sayThey have a share in the world to come
ThenThen your tradition honours the righteous of every people. The Quran says the like in 2:62.
If you sayThey are held to the seven laws of Noah
ThenThen God has dealings with them, and they have a way to Him outside the particular covenant. That widens the question.
If you sayI am not sure
ThenIt is worth looking into. You will find passages from your own tradition after this Step.

Translation of the meaning

And among the people of Moses is a community[412] which guides by truth and by it establishes justice.

Translator's notes

[412] Those of them who accepted and followed the final prophet, Muḥammad (ﷺ).

Quran · Al-A'raf 7:159

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقْنَـٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرٍ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلْنَـٰكُمْ شُعُوبًا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ أَكْرَمَكُمْ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتْقَىٰكُمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allāh is the most righteous[1521] of you. Indeed, Allāh is Knowing and Aware.

Translator's notes

[1521] Literally, "he who has the most taqwā," i.e., consciousness and fear of Allāh, piety and righteousness.

Quran · Al-Hujurat 49:13

Translation

He made from one blood every nation of men to dwell on all the surface of the earth, having determined appointed seasons and the boundaries of their dwellings,

Original · Ancient Greek

ἐποίησέν τε ἐξ ἑνὸς πᾶν ἔθνος ἀνθρώπων κατοικεῖν ἐπὶ παντὸς προσώπου τῆς γῆς, ὁρίσας προστεταγμένους καιροὺς καὶ τὰς ὁροθεσίας τῆς κατοικίας αὐτῶν,

Acts · 17:26

World English Bible

The Quran does not stop there. It says that among Moses's people there is a community that guides by truth and does justice by it. The second verse then widens to all humankind: made from a male and a female, into peoples and tribes so that you may know one another, the noblest being the most reverent, and God knows. So no people can claim nobility by birth, and none can deny it to another.

A question for you

What is one thing your people has to teach another people, and one thing it has to learn from them?
